findings.source: IlkRegistry.sol:119 mapping (bytes32 => Ilk) public ilkData; Ilk.name (slot +4), Ilk.symbol (slot +5); :370 return ilkData[ilk].name; :250 ilkData[ilk].name = data
findings.issue: The string members name/symbol are printed as raw stor[sha3(ilk, 4) + 4] / + 5 (and their data as stor[sha3(sha3(ilk, 4) + 4)]), while the same words are class[ilk].field_1024 / field_1032 / field_1280 elsewhere, so one member has two spellings. In add and put the slot is also carried in mem[0] (sha3(mem[0]) for the name, sha3(_8 + 5) for the symbol).
findings.rule: A slot sha3(k, B) + i, with B a mapping-of-struct base and i inside the struct, is member i of B[k] whatever the access (.length, data at sha3(slot)); forward mem[0] = e into a later sha3(mem[0]) when mem[0] is not written in between.

findings.source: IlkRegistry.sol:119 public ilkData getter (7 words + 2 strings); :302-323 info returns (name, symbol, class, dec, gem, pip, join, xlip)
findings.issue: A return of static words and two strings is left as raw 'return memory' after 40-50 lines of hand-encoded heads, offsets and tails (the second string copied by a P7 while); the one-string getters name()/symbol() are printed as return Array(len=..., data=...). info also duplicates the symbol load in both arms of 'if not name.length' (P12, 10 lines).
findings.rule: Recognize a returned region made of a head (static words, and offsets equal to the distance to each tail) followed by length-prefixed, zero-padded tails as an ABI tuple and print its members; merge equal arm tails.

findings.source: IlkRegistry.sol:187 require(ilks.length < uint96(-1), "IlkRegistry/too-many-ilks"); :286-292 bytes32[] memory _ilks = new bytes32[](end - start + 1); ... return _ilks
findings.issue: _95 is mem[64] read one line earlier with no write in between, yet _95 - mem[64] is not folded, so the revert is not shown as 'IlkRegistry/too-many-ilks'; list's return is raw memory although mem[64] and mem[128] (= end - start + 1) were set at lines 179-180. The same unresolved pointer makes the gem()/dec()/symbol() calls P2 and the Ilk struct's members slices (uint96(...field_0) = mem[_92 + 20 len 12]).
findings.rule: Two reads of mem[64] with no write to it in between are equal (and a read after mem[64] = e is e); with that, e - mem[64] folds and the Error(string) and return-array recognizers apply. Same root as c00178 and c00228.

findings.issue: The whole-slot clears of slot 0 (pos + join) and slot 2 (class + pip) print as writes to their first member, which reads as clearing pos and class only (P15).
findings.rule: Print a whole-word write of a slot that holds several members as one write per member (field_0 = 0, field_96 = 0) or as the slot itself.

findings.source: IlkRegistry.sol:250 ilkData[ilk].name = data (storage string overwrite); :270 delete ilkData[ilk]
findings.issue: The old string length and the clearing of its stale tail slots are spelled out arithmetically, although the text reads the same storage word as .length everywhere else.
findings.rule: (w & (256 * (1 - (w & 1)) - 1)) / 2 is the byte length of the storage string whose length word is w: print it as the old value's .length, and stor[S len -S + max(S + n, S)] as stor[S len n] when S + n cannot wrap.

findings.source: IlkRegistry.sol:100 VatLike public immutable vat; GemInfo public immutable gemInfo
findings.issue: solc immutables vat and gemInfo read as 0. Because both are address 0, the extcodesize checks of the try calls gemInfo.name/symbol (present in the bytecode at 0xfc1) are rightly dropped as implied by the vat.wards check. Not a decompiler error.

notes: All 31 ABI functions present and reviewed; no semantic error found. Source loops: bytes32ToStr's for (inlined twice in add, both whiles; the second keeps 'assert idx < mem[_38]' although mem[_38] = 32, P11) and list(uint256,uint256)'s for (while; its two asserts are implied by start <= end < length, P11). The 5 other whiles are ABI copies (P7: add's two string decodes, ilkData, info, list's return). bytes32ToStr's loop writes byte(i, w) to mem[p + i] for i < 32, i.e. mem[p len 32] = w, which a copy rule could show. add line 621 'revert with Error(string reason), 32, 36, ..., mem[232 len 28]' is exact: solc 0.6.12 codecopies the 36-byte message, so the padding is the dog.ilks return data left in memory. put's name copy keeps its zero padding as mem[_name.length + 448 len ...] while the symbol's prints Bytes(..., 0). list(): max(192, 32 * n + 160) under 'if n' is 32 * n + 160. Storage: 'class' names the Ilk mapping after the getter of one member (P13). Event parameter names come from the database (File(bytes32 name, bytes32 nftID_, ...)).
summary: Faithful text with both source loops as while; the struct's string members print as raw stor[sha3(ilk, 4) + 4], the two-string getters end in raw 'return memory', and an unresolved free pointer hides one revert message, one array return, four calls (P2) and the struct written by add.
